thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected for /v1/stream (region: us-west-2). SLO breach detected (p99 > 2.5s)
ops-bot: Paging on-call: @ana @dave. Autoscale did not absorb the surge, KV eviction rate spiked.
ana: on it, pulling metrics now. grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/stream_latency/7490012345
dave: seeing streaming stalls + backlog on decode workers. p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.2s right now.
sophia: is this the same prefill/decode imbalance we saw last month?
ana: looking at KV cache heatmap — lots of small slab evictions, fragmentation visible. prefills are queuing, decode workers idle occasionally.
matt: logs show repeated prefill->decode handoff timeouts: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z prefill: enq req_id=abcd delay=0.24s
2026-03-15T10:12:07Z prefill: send to decode req_id=abcd wait=1.02s
2026-03-15T10:12:08Z decode: missing kv fragment for req_id=abcd, fallback miss
```
ana: key observation: prefill throughput temporarily outpaces decode capacity for long-context requests, causing hot keys to be evicted and then re-prefilled -> extra IO and tail stalls.
dave: confirmed. KV eviction_count up 3.5x in last 5m, slab-alloc churn high.
sophia: immediate mitigation options?
matt: list: 1) throttle prefill for long requests (reduce prefill concurrency) 2) bump decode worker replicas for streaming pool 3) temporarily increase KV slab reservation for streaming_tier 4) route highest-latency tenants to fallback smaller model 5) force a controlled eviction smoothing (lower eviction aggressiveness)
ana: doing 1 & 3 now. lowering prefill concurrency for requests with seq_len>1024 from 32->8. executing: `kcctl set prefill.max_concurrency 8 --selector=streaming_tier`
ops-bot: Command accepted, rolling config to streaming nodes (16 nodes).
dave: I'm scaling decode pool replicas +2 in us-west-2 (should hit ~60s to allocate).
sophia: pushing KV slab bump: `kvctl reserve --pool streaming_tier --mb 2048` — doing a rolling increase of reserved slab to reduce fragmentation.
ana: monitoring effects. initial delta after prefill throttle: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 2.6s in 60s. eviction_rate down 28%.
matt: good. decode replicas still warming; streaming stalls still present for some tails.
dave: for the subset of requests still stalling, adding a policy to route >90th-percentile token-length requests to fallback-model-small which has lower memory working set to avoid extra KV misses. applying routing rule now.
ana: routing rule applied. sample traffic shows those requests now have p99 ~1.4s.
sophia: customer impact? any marked errors or user-visible timeouts?
matt: no errors, just elevated latency and occasional streaming stall -> clients see pauses. handful of customers reported slow UI updates (support ticket links: https://support.internal/t/INC-4321).
dave: triage severity -> Sev2 (partial degraded experience, multiple customers). ops-bot: severity set to Sev2 and notified CS.
ana: jotting short mitigation timeline: 10:12 alert -> 10:15 prefill throttle -> 10:16 slab bump -> 10:17 decode scale -> 10:18 routing rules -> 10:20 measurable p99 improvement.
sophia: any quick config to prevent re-fragmentation after slab bump? maybe increase min-slab-size or alter allocator thresholds.
matt: yes, follow-up: change allocator.min_slab_kb from 128->256 for streaming_tier, but that's a riskier change; schedule for controlled rollout after this is stable.
dave: agree. we'll keep that for next maintenance window, not live now.
ana: handoff: my shift ends in 25m. @dave, you'll take the on-call until 14:00 UTC?
dave: I can take it. I'll watch for reversion of p99 and eviction rates. setting a watch: `alertctl watch p99_stream >2s for 5m`
ops-bot: Handoff recorded. oncall: dave (until 14:00 UTC).
sophia: post-incident actions (short): 1) postmortem draft with timeline and config diffs 2) run replay of heavy long-context traffic against local env to reproduce fragmentation 3) plan allocator tuning and prefill safety caps 4) customer comms slate for impacted customers
matt: I'll open the incident issue: https://issues.internal/RED-INC-2026-03-kv-prefill-imbalance (assigned to eng-runtime).
ana: one more note — add a test to the integration suite to simulate prefill burst vs decode slowdowns and assert eviction_rate stays under threshold.
dave: will monitor. if p99 rises >2.5s again, escalate to Sev1 and enable emergency fallback (route all streaming->fallback-model-small).
sophia: thanks team. leaving detailed logs and the grafana panels in the incident issue. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident update logged (RED-INC-2026-03-kv-prefill-imbalance). Next update due in 30m.
